claim_ceiling: This artifact treats causal inversion as a research method for reading textual and museum-provenance sequences. It does not claim that real-world time, entropy, or causality is physically inverted, and it does not authenticate any surviving object as the literal phallus of Osiris.

book_of_dead_inversion_rule.do_not_do: Do not simply read modern chapter numbers from 165 down to 1 and call that ancient inversion.
book_of_dead_inversion_rule.reason: The Book of the Dead is a repertoire of roughly two hundred formulae; ancient manuscripts contain selections, order varies, and modern chapter numbering is a scholarly reference system. The causal inversion therefore acts on dependencies and outcomes, not on modern numbering.
book_of_dead_inversion_rule.method: Start at the desired terminal state (survival, restoration, emergence), then move backward through prerequisites: stability -> reassembly -> body-part identity -> protection/container -> burial/loss context.

inverse_pilot_graph.evidence: Formula for not dying again; terminal condition is restored persistence.
Gold djed formula addresses Osiris with 'Raise yourself'; stabilization follows restoration.
Protective sons of Horus state that bones and limbs are united/assembled and the heart is brought back and placed in the body.
The body is mapped to deities; explicitly, the phallus is that of Osiris. This is an identity/function node, not a physical-location statement.

The composition includes the gloss 'yesterday is Osiris, tomorrow is Ra' and identifies Anubis as guarding a chest containing the entrails of Osiris. This supplies a textual time-bridge and a container motif, but not proof of a hidden phallus container.

The formula says the one in the chest is well and identifies the one in the chest as Osiris N. This justifies searching container/reliquary language but cannot be literalized into a specific relic without provenance.

The burial formula places Osiris in a funerary/judgement context and mentions mourning women at the Two Riverbanks of the Washermen. It is a ritual-geographic anchor, not coordinates for the lost organ.

pilot_result.inverse_chain: SURVIVE -> STABILIZE/RAISE -> REASSEMBLE -> IDENTIFY_BODY_PARTS -> PROTECT/CONTAIN -> BURIAL_CONTEXT -> EARLIER_LOSS_EVENT
pilot_result.important_observation: The inverse pass repeatedly moves from restored whole to protected/contained body and only then toward burial/loss context. This makes hidden-container testing methodologically reasonable, but does not establish that Seth or another agent hid a literal relic in a statue.
next_text_pass: Expand the same dependency extraction across regeneration chapters 17-63.
Expand across underworld/protection chapters 130-162, prioritizing container, chest, sealed chamber, reassembly, Djed, body integrity, Osiris and body-part language.
Keep manuscript-specific ordering separate from modern chapter numbering.

hidden_container_hypothesis.user_hypothesis_as_testable_branch: A relic or substitute might have been deliberately preserved inside a sealed cavity, reliquary, statuette, mummy packet, or nested container, potentially under a generic museum label.
hidden_container_hypothesis.reason: Ancient Egyptian objects can be hollow and can contain organic or ritual material, but no evidence in this pass establishes an engineered vacuum capsule.

non_destructive_imaging_gate.admission_rule: Promote only if imaging reveals a distinct internal object/packet/cavity AND the parent object's provenance/function is independently Osirian. A cavity alone is not a relic signal.

imaging_precedents.source: The Metropolitan Museum of Art object 25.2.11
imaging_precedents.finding: A hollow Egyptian bronze falcon statue was shown by X-radiography to contain animal bones; a sealed insertion opening exists beneath the tail.
imaging_precedents.methodological_use: Demonstrates that a statue-like Egyptian object can conceal contents that are only evident non-destructively.

imaging_precedents.finding: CT/X-ray inspection showed linen scraps and a wooden stick rather than expected baboon skeletal material.
imaging_precedents.methodological_use: Demonstrates that external form can mislead and internal imaging can overturn the label-level expectation.

imaging_precedents.finding: Radiography/CT were used on a resin-encrusted linen packet; results were partly inconclusive and later material analysis refined interpretation.
imaging_precedents.methodological_use: Demonstrates both the value and limitation of CT: ambiguity must remain ambiguity until other analyses resolve it.

imaging_precedents.source: 2024 study of a hollow-cast bronze Osiris statue in the Egyptian Museum, Cairo
imaging_precedents.finding: X-ray radiography, XRF and XRD were used non-destructively to characterize a hollow-cast Osiris statue and its hidden construction/polychromy features.
imaging_precedents.methodological_use: Directly validates radiographic audit of Osiris statuary as a technically realistic museum-research path.

fish_branch.rule: The Plutarch/fish episode is retained as a late literary/mythic witness, not imposed as a biological fact or search gate.
fish_branch.why: No empirical material properties of a divine organ are available, so statements about whether fish could digest, damage, desire, fear, or refuse it are not testable. The research search therefore neither requires belief in the fish episode nor deletes it from the source ledger.
fish_branch.search_effect: Do not restrict the hunt to fish remains or fish cults. Keep fish objects only as matched contextual controls unless independent Osirian relic evidence converges.
